design.affected_system: housing inspection, code enforcement, repair, and tenant-support system
alternatives: advance high-risk work within verified feasible windows for housing inspection, enforcement, and repair schedule
use rolling risk and capacity updates to reschedule housing inspection, enforcement, and repair schedule
pair severity-, dependency-, and statutory-deadline scheduling with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Complaints, inspections, violations, ownership, repair, and closure records retain distinct semantics.
Tenant vulnerability and building condition are measured only from authorized, documented sources.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: continue the fixed operating calendar for housing inspection, enforcement, and repair schedule.

constraints.description: The housing habitability and code operations schedule must respect declared labor, access, sequencing, notice, and completion windows.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_question: When should initial inspections, rechecks, legal notices, repairs, and tenant support occur?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The housing habitability and code operations schedule must respect declared labor, access, sequencing, notice, and completion windows.
independence_key.decision_object: housing inspection, enforcement, and repair schedule
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for housing inspection, enforcement, and repair schedule passes documented checks for effective dates, time zones, calendars, lead times, completion semantics, and update cadence.
independence_key.primary_outcome: priority case-days beyond lawful response deadlines

design.intended_claim: A versioned schedule design for comparing declared alternatives affecting housing inspection, enforcement, and repair schedule, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: priority case-days beyond lawful response deadlines
distributional gap in priority case-days beyond lawful response deadlines
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not infer completed inspection, notice, repair, or safe occupancy from a scheduled task.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for housing inspection, enforcement, and repair schedule passes documented checks for effective dates, time zones, calendars, lead times, completion semantics, and update cadence.

design.title: Schedule housing inspections, follow-ups, and repairs
transportability_risks: Housing law, tenure, building age, complaint access, inspection practice, and enforcement differ.
Complaint records may over- or under-represent physical conditions and retaliation risk.

family.affected_system: housing inspection, code enforcement, repair, and tenant-support system
claim_boundary: Requests, listings, parcels, and administrative records do not alone verify conditions or need.
Screened sites and portfolios are not permits, acquisitions, adopted plans, or completed housing.
Displacement, affordability, habitability, and program effects require direct outcomes and identification.
family.description: Eight decisions for condition-signal diagnosis, inspection forecasting, repair portfolios, service access, inspector allocation, case scheduling, surge stress, and enforcement evaluation.
family.title: Housing habitability and code operations

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
